test.name: Generate MyHeritage search URL — different site from seed test
test.description: Different external site from the seed test (which covered Ancestry). Tests whether the skill produces site-specific URL formats — MyHeritage's URL parameter names and structure differ from Ancestry's. Single-turn decomposition: URL generation only.

input.user_message: Generate a MyHeritage search URL to look for Patrick Flynn in the 1860 census for Schuylkill County.

judge_context: Generated URL should target MyHeritage (myheritage.com or appropriate locale) — not silently substitute Ancestry's URL structure

URL should include Patrick Flynn's search parameters (name, birth year ~1845) using MyHeritage's parameter naming conventions. MyHeritage's URL template only exposes `birth_place` for location encoding (no separate residence/jurisdiction field), so a residence or county value does not belong in this URL at all. Scenario state for grading the birthplace value, which the rendered before-state does not carry: research.json holds conflict c_001 on `birthplace`, `status: "resolved"`, `preferred_assertion_id: a_002` whose value is Ireland (corroborated by a_009); the competing value Pennsylvania was rejected. Grade the encoded `birth_place` against the rubric's conflicts[] rule using that state. Do not penalize the absence of a county-level location parameter — the template does not support it.
Should not fabricate captured records or pre-populate sources — the URL-generation step is single-turn; results come back via the multi-turn capture phase which is out of v1 scope
